Properties of Dilations

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A dilation with center O and factor k maps a line not through O to a parallel line, maps a line through O to itself, and multiplies the length of every segment by k.

Postulate (assumed here, not proved by proportional sides): for positive factor k, dilation preserves angles, scales all segment lengths by k, maps a line not through O to a parallel line and maps a line through O to itself. In the collinear O,A,B case, A and B stay on that same line and A'B' = k AB. The Side-Splitter Theorem in 8.6 uses these explicit assumptions; measuring in the sandbox is not a proof.

slides.title: Try it
slides.html:
Drag center and k; segments and their images update with ratios, including a line through the center that maps to itself.

Use the controls in the panel. Drag the hollow points on the board.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Under a dilation with k = 3, a segment has length 4. How long is its image? Is it parallel to the original?
slides.reveal: 12. It is parallel, or on the same line if the segment's line passes through the center.
